prompt:
Photograph, straight on, of a tall rectangular display board filling the
whole picture: a heavy frame of dark carved pewter with a beaded inner
edge, and inside it deep crimson velvet. On the velvet hang three
period swords side by side, upright, hilts at the top and points down,
well apart, each plainly different: on the left a rapier with a
needle-thin blade no wider than a pencil and a swept hilt of looping
blued steel bars and rings around the grip; in the middle a short broad
cutlass with a curved blade and a brass shell guard; on the right a
heavy broadsword with a wide straight double-edged blade, three times
as wide as the rapier's, with a long gilded cross guard, a leather grip
and a round gilded pommel at the top; its blade narrows to a single
sharp point at the bottom, with nothing below the point. Each sword has
one hilt only, at its top. Even museum light, sharp focus,
realistic. Style: one consistent look for the whole series, photographed like a
period film still of the 1660s Caribbean, natural warm light, gentle
film grain, muted rich colours with warm amber and deep teal tones,
moderate contrast, shallow depth of field, realistic textures, no text.
